newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end down as investors lose confidence.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end down as investors lose confidence.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed down in low volume Monday as investor worries about the country's slow economic growth were compounded by delays to the government's long-awaited Brady Plan closing, brokers said.
After a trend over the last few months of slipping prices and low volumes, brokers said they did not expect any good news in the short-term to lift the market.
Monday, the General Index fell 1.43 percent to 1,422.7 points, and the blue-chip Selective Index dropped 1.16 percent to 1,991.0 points, according to preliminary stock figures.

"There is no positive news that can change the poor expectations caused by the fall in the economic growth rate and the postponement of December's Brady closing," said Jaime Jara of local brokerage Inversion y Desarrollo.
After several months of slow growth, the government estimates the economy will grow around 2.5 percent this year, down from 7.0 percent last year.
Also, last week the government said it could not be sure of closing its Brady Plan to restructure the bulk of its commercial debt on December 22 as scheduled.
Brokers also said the consensus among players was that while the market would see the occasional, small technical rebound, it would not see any real recovery until 1997.

Monday, benchmark Telefonica del Peru closed down 1.94 percent to 5.06 soles, in volume of 1.415 million shares, according to preliminary figures. Electricity distributor Luz del Sur, which saw the sale of the state's 30 percent stake in the company start last week, fell 3.68 percent to 3.40 soles on volume of 219,000 shares.
In a total of 1,015 trades, volume was estimated at 19.1 million soles ($7.4 million)
